title: 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System
description: 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System Solicitation Closes at 02 :00 PM on 26 October 2026 Time Zone EDT RETURN BIDS TO: NRC.BidReceiving-ReceptiondesSoumissions.CNRC@nrc-cnrc.gc.ca Statement of Requirement Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System. The National Research Council of Canada’s (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation (CDI), part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL), requires one (1) integrated topo bathymetric LiDAR system deployable from NRC’s medium class Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) to support research, development, testing, method validation, and operational deployments. The system must capture above water topography and shallow water bathymetry within a single factory integrated payload and deliver survey grade outputs through a manufacturer supported hydrographic processing workflow. BACKGROUND: LiDAR is used to generate high accuracy topographic data and digital elevation models by measuring precise distances between a sensor and target surfaces. Conventional topographic LiDAR typically operates at near infrared wavelengths that do not penetrate water, so surveys end at the water surface. To characterize shorelines and other shallow water features within a single survey, a topo bathymetric capability is required to detect both the water surface and submerged bottom under suitable conditions. To support dual use applications such as shoreline mapping, shallow water target detection, wildfire resource assessment, infrastructure inspection, emergency response, and evaluation of potential autonomous landing sites, the Remote Sensing Imaging Group (RSIG) within the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL) requires an integrated topo bathymetric LiDAR system deployable from NRC’s medium class RPAS. RSIG, with support from NRC’s Design and Fabrication Department and the Flight Research Laboratory Instrumentation Group, will integrate the system on NRC platforms. Given the field based, survey grade nature of the work, dependable vendor support, training, and documentation are required to maintain operational readiness and minimize downtime, reduce technical risk, and maintain continuity of operations. 1.0 Requirement: Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-deployable integrated topographic and bathymetric (topo-bathymetric) LiDAR system (the system), quantity one (1) Specifications: The system must: 1.1 Integrated topo-bathymetric capability -collect both topographic and bathymetric LiDAR data using a single integrated payload 1.2 Bathymetric green laser -use a green laser wavelength (532 nm) providing both terrestrial measurements and water-surface and sub-aqueous bottom returns. 1.3 Unconditional full-waveform recording -record the full return waveform unconditionally for every emitted laser pulse, so that weak submerged-bottom echoes can be recovered, averaged, and reprocessed rather than being permanently lost when they fall below a real-time detection threshold 1.4 Measurement rate and multi-target capability -provide user-selectable measurement rates of up to at least 200 kHz, record at least 15 target returns per emitted pulse, and provide 16-bit intensity information. 1.5 Selectable beam divergence -provide user-selectable laser-beam divergence, adjustable over a range of at least 1 mrad to 6 mrad, so that acquisition can be optimized for different flight altitudes, water clarity, and turbidity conditions. 1.6 Water penetration -be capable of penetrating a minimum of 2 m of clear water under zero-turbidity conditions. 1.7 Scanning field of view - provide an effective scanning field of view of at least 40 degrees perpendicular to the flight direction, equivalent to an off-nadir scan angle of at least 20 degrees, suitable for RPAS topo-bathymetric mapping. 1.8 Integrated survey-grade GNSS/INS - include a fully integrated Global Navigation Satellite System / Inertial Navigation System (GNSS/INS) providing, after post-processing, horizontal position accuracy of 5 cm or better, vertical position accuracy of 10 cm or better, roll and pitch accuracy of 0.02 degrees or better, and heading accuracy of 0.05 degrees or better. The GNSS/INS must be compatible with NRC’s existing Applanix POSPac trajectory post-processing workflow and must be supplied with the required post-processing software licence. 1.9 Integrated RGB camera - include an integrated, co-aligned RGB camera with a minimum resolution of 20 megapixels, supporting co-registration of the LiDAR data with true-colour imagery for draped surface products, structure-from-motion applications, and three-dimensional surface visualization 1.10 Onboard data storage - include internal solid-state data storage and support removable storage media. 1.11 Environmental protection - be suitable for outdoor field operations and provide protection against dust and environmental moisture appropriate for RPAS-based operations, with an ingress protection rating of at least IP64. 1.12 Operating environment - be suitable for operation in Canadian outdoor field conditions, including ambient temperatures below freezing down to -10 °C, and withstand storage and transportation at temperatures down to -20 °C. 1.13 Hydrographic processing software - include manufacturer-supported software covering the complete RPAS-based topo-bathymetric workflow, including: mission planning; system operation and data acquisition; data download and management; inertial data processing; kinematic LiDAR data processing; system calibration; water-surface modelling; correction of underwater measurements for refraction and light-travel time; full-waveform bathymetric analysis; RGB image processing; rigorous data adjustment; quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC); and export of processed data products to commonly used formats, including LAS. 1.14 Calibration - be delivered with system boresight calibration and digital camera calibration completed, together with the applicable calibration documentation for the integrated sensing components. 1.15 Technical Documentation - provide a comprehensive technical manual, including diagrams and/or procedures for troubleshooting and performing basic maintenance tasks. 1.16 RPAS compatibility The complete sensor payload must be suitable for deployment on medium-class RPAS, must have a total payload weight not exceeding 12 kg, and must be capable of integration on NRC’s medium-class RPAS through appropriate mechanical, electrical, and communications interfaces, and must operate from a DC power supply of 18–34 VDC. 1.17 Manufacturer repairs All repairs and recalibration must be performed at the manufacturer’s facility or by a manufacturer-authorized service provider, with documentation provided following each repair or recalibration. 2.0 Training: The Contractor must provide comprehensive RPAS-based topo-bathymetric operations and workflow training for up to four (4) NRC personnel covering, at minimum: • mission planning; • system operation and data acquisition; • operational best practices; • data download; • inertial data processing; • refraction correction; • LiDAR and image data processing; • full-waveform bathymetric analysis; • data quality assurance and • quality control (QA/QC); and export of processed data products. The location of the training to be determined following integration of the system on an NRC RPAS. 3.0 Warranty and Support: 3.1 Warranty The system and all supplied hardware must include a minimum twelve (12) month manufacturer’s warranty covering material and manufacturing defects and operation within the manufacturer’s specifications, commencing upon acceptance of the goods. title: Question/Answer #2 RFP 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System
description: 21 October 2026, Question and Answer #2 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System Please see tender documents for details _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 20 October 2026, Question and Answer #1 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System Please see tender documents for details _____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________ 26-58124 Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System Solicitation Closes at 02 :00 PM on 26 October 2026 Time Zone EDT RETURN BIDS TO: NRC.BidReceiving-ReceptiondesSoumissions.CNRC@nrc-cnrc.gc.ca Statement of Requirement Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-Deployable Integrated Topographic and Bathymetric (Topo-Bathymetric) LiDAR System. The National Research Council of Canada’s (NRC) Centre for Drone Innovation (CDI), part of the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL), requires one (1) integrated topo bathymetric LiDAR system deployable from NRC’s medium class Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) to support research, development, testing, method validation, and operational deployments. The system must capture above water topography and shallow water bathymetry within a single factory integrated payload and deliver survey grade outputs through a manufacturer supported hydrographic processing workflow. BACKGROUND: LiDAR is used to generate high accuracy topographic data and digital elevation models by measuring precise distances between a sensor and target surfaces. Conventional topographic LiDAR typically operates at near infrared wavelengths that do not penetrate water, so surveys end at the water surface. To characterize shorelines and other shallow water features within a single survey, a topo bathymetric capability is required to detect both the water surface and submerged bottom under suitable conditions. To support dual use applications such as shoreline mapping, shallow water target detection, wildfire resource assessment, infrastructure inspection, emergency response, and evaluation of potential autonomous landing sites, the Remote Sensing Imaging Group (RSIG) within the Drone and Flight Autonomy Laboratory (DFAL) requires an integrated topo bathymetric LiDAR system deployable from NRC’s medium class RPAS. RSIG, with support from NRC’s Design and Fabrication Department and the Flight Research Laboratory Instrumentation Group, will integrate the system on NRC platforms. Given the field based, survey grade nature of the work, dependable vendor support, training, and documentation are required to maintain operational readiness and minimize downtime, reduce technical risk, and maintain continuity of operations. 1.0 Requirement: Remotely Piloted Aircraft System (RPAS)-deployable integrated topographic and bathymetric (topo-bathymetric) LiDAR system (the system), quantity one (1) Specifications: The system must: 1.1 Integrated topo-bathymetric capability -collect both topographic and bathymetric LiDAR data using a single integrated payload 1.2 Bathymetric green laser -use a green laser wavelength (532 nm) providing both terrestrial measurements and water-surface and sub-aqueous bottom returns. 1.3 Unconditional full-waveform recording -record the full return waveform unconditionally for every emitted laser pulse, so that weak submerged-bottom echoes can be recovered, averaged, and reprocessed rather than being permanently lost when they fall below a real-time detection threshold 1.4 Measurement rate and multi-target capability -provide user-selectable measurement rates of up to at least 200 kHz, record at least 15 target returns per emitted pulse, and provide 16-bit intensity information. 1.5 Selectable beam divergence -provide user-selectable laser-beam divergence, adjustable over a range of at least 1 mrad to 6 mrad, so that acquisition can be optimized for different flight altitudes, water clarity, and turbidity conditions. 1.6 Water penetration -be capable of penetrating a minimum of 2 m of clear water under zero-turbidity conditions. 1.7 Scanning field of view - provide an effective scanning field of view of at least 40 degrees perpendicular to the flight direction, equivalent to an off-nadir scan angle of at least 20 degrees, suitable for RPAS topo-bathymetric mapping. 1.8 Integrated survey-grade GNSS/INS - include a fully integrated Global Navigation Satellite System / Inertial Navigation System (GNSS/INS) providing, after post-processing, horizontal position accuracy of 5 cm or better, vertical position accuracy of 10 cm or better, roll and pitch accuracy of 0.02 degrees or better, and heading accuracy of 0.05 degrees or better. title: SOFTWARE LICENSING OPPORTUNITY: CorrelateIQ - Correlation-Based System Intelligence
description: CorrelateIQ reveals hidden relationships among many data streams at once, catching hidden patterns, early warning signs and operating shifts that single-variable monitoring overlooks. Built on analysis techniques from high-energy physics, this software from Los Alamos National Laboratory turns existing sensor and process data into practical insight that helps organizations prevent failures, protect quality and reduce downtime. Because the method makes no assumptions about where the data comes from, it applies to a wide range of numeric data, from manufacturing sensors and equipment logs to financial records, market data and scientific measurements. Overview Factories, laboratories, infrastructure networks, financial and real-estate markets now produce huge volumes of linked data from sensors, equipment logs and transactions. Most analytics tools, however, judge each variable separately or depend on fixed thresholds that trigger an alert only after a single reading crosses a limit. These methods have trouble spotting effects that arise from subtle interactions among many variables, such as gradual equipment wear, a drifting manufacturing process or a market entering a new phase. As a result, organizations often miss the earliest warning signals, react to failures only after they happen and leave much of the value in their data untapped. Teams in every data-reach fields need a practical way of understanding how an entire system behaves as a whole, not merely how each part performs alone. Key Benefits Spots early warning signs before small problems become costly failures Uncovers the hidden factors that drive outcomes such as quality, risk or price Reveals relationships across many data sources that conventional tools miss Identifies which combinations of variables matter most Gets more value from data organizations already collect Works across industries and data types, from factory sensors to financial records Condenses complex, high-volume data into clear, compact indicators Complements existing monitoring, machine learning and digital twin systems Core Capabilities At its core, CorrelateIQ: Correlation-Based System Intelligence measures collective behavior. Users choose the variables or signals of interest, and the software calculates higher-order correlations that capture how those inputs change together rather than separately. The framework accepts mixed data types, including time-series records, sensor readings, transactional data and scientific measurements. It condenses them into compact representations of overall system behavior. Because the software reduces many interacting variables to a smaller set of meaningful indicators, complex environments become easier to read, compare and act upon. CorrelateIQ also goes beyond a single snapshot. It tracks how correlation patterns change over time, so users can see shifts in operating state, new anomalies and transitions from one regime to another. Its outputs can act as an analytics or feature-generation layer that feeds existing monitoring, control or machine learning systems. It can run in real-time monitoring pipelines or offline analytics platforms. Planned improvements include automated selection and ranking of the most useful correlations, adaptive correlation building and closer integration with predictive maintenance and digital twin workflows. Use Cases & Market Applications Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing (process monitoring, quality control) Industrial operations and energy (predictive maintenance, equipment health) Infrastructure (structural health monitoring, multisensor networks) Industrial software and digital twins (system modeling, feature generation) Finance and real estate (market shift detection, risk analysis) Scientific research (physics data analysis, complex systems studies) Healthcare, transportation and cybersecurity (anomaly detection, early warning) Supply chains and climate monitoring (leading indicators, change detection) LA-UR-26-29216 LANL Tech Partnerships: Unlock the Innovative Potential Los Alamos National Laboratory offers a wide range of cutting-edge technologies and capabilities that may provide your company with a competitive edge in the market and unlock the innovative potential that can enhance, refine, and revolutionize your products. LANL�s licensing program focuses on moving inventions developed by our researchers to commercial innovations. Patented and patent pending inventions and copyrighted software are available to existing and start-up companies through exclusive and non-exclusive licensing agreements. For specific discussions, please contact licensing@lanl.gov. Note: This is not a call for external services for the development of this technology. https://www.lanl.gov/engage/collaboration/feynman-center/partner-with-us/licensing-technology m.lanl.gov/tech-search

title: Ireland – E-learning services – TR5866 A Single Supplier Framework Agreement Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services pursuant to a framework agreement
description: The Contracting Entity intends to procure a Digital Learning Design, Development and Maintenance Services framework for the provision of specialist digital learning services, including instructional design, eLearning development, accessibility reviews, project management and associated support services. The successful tenderer will be required to work collaboratively with Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and stakeholders to design, develop, review, test and deliver digital learning content from initial onboarding through to final approval and provision of SCORM-compliant outputs. The supplier will be expected to provide a structured and transparent development methodology, supported by appropriate governance, project management, universal design principles including accessibility, quality assurance and stakeholder engagement processes. It is proposed that the Framework will include (non-exhaustive list – high level scope): Create engaging, accessible and effective digital learning that keeps learner needs, content and learning objectives central to the design. Examples of digital learning topics and types include: Policy, process or compliance learning Systems, technical or operational training Bite-sized learning, such as microlearning, video or animation Develop digital learning materials using the ADDIE (Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation and Evaluation) framework, ensuring learning objectives, activities and assessments align with Bloom’s Taxonomy and the needs of the target audience. Use purposeful interactive approaches to enhance learner engagement. Apply Universal Design for Learning (UDL) and accessibility by design principles throughout, ensuring compliance with WCAG 2.2, EN 301 549 and ESB accessibility requirements, and meeting accessibility best practices. Ensure all interactive elements are accessible, usable and support diverse learner needs, undertaking additional development where required to meet accessibility requirements. INTRODUCTION The Aircraft Project Management Office (AIR PMO), under the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager Robotic Autonomous Systems (DRPM RAS), is conducting market research regarding commercially available and emerging Group 1 and Group 2 Unmanned Aircraft System (UAS) Training, Mission Planning, Mission Rehearsal, Simulation, and Qualification Management Systems. For market research and planning purposes, the Government is seeking information regarding industry�s ability to provide and support these capabilities at scale. Potential future demand could involve thousands of training devices, simulator stations, software licenses, or equivalent deployed units. However, no procurement quantity, acquisition strategy, or requirement has been established, and any quantities referenced in this RFI are illustrative planning assumptions only. The Government requests white papers from interested parties with commercially available or emerging capabilities. Responses will assist the Government in identifying potential solutions; understanding technical approaches, system maturity, interoperability, scalability, implementation considerations, and business models; refining capability objectives and potential requirements; and informing acquisition planning and potential procurement strategies. This RFI follows the Air PMO virtual Industry Day conducted on 03 September 2026. Participation in the Industry Day is not a prerequisite for responding to this RFI. Interested parties may respond regardless of whether they attended the event. This RFI is an independent Air PMO market research effort and is not associated with or conducted in support of the Drone Dominance Program. Respondents should address the capability areas and information requested in this RFI without assuming any relationship to that program�s requirements, acquisition approach, funding, schedule, or procurement quantities. BACKGROUND Simulation-based training has the potential to enhance operator proficiency, improve training availability, increase training throughput, reduce operational risk, and provide realistic Mission Planning and Mission Rehearsal capabilities for Group 1 and Group 2 UAS. These capabilities may enable operators to safely practice in realistic and challenging operational and threat environments, emergency procedures, and degraded system behaviors that may be impractical, unsafe, or cost-prohibitive to execute using live aircraft. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. ACCESS TO SOLICITATION DOCUMENTS AND CLASSIFIED DATA The AN/BYG-1 Applications solicitation, Statement of Work (SOW), and associated unclassified attachments are designated as Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and will not be posted directly to SAM.gov. These documents will be made available exclusively via the secure Electronic Technical Information Center (E-TIC) portal hosted by the Advanced Interactive Management Technology Center (AIMTC). Additionally, portions of the Government Furnished Information, specifically, the classified software source code provided to support proposal development are classified at the SECRET level and will be transmitted physically. Documents made available during this procurement may contain classified data and/or technical data whose export is restricted by the Arms Export Control Act. Foreign participation shall be limited by applicable legal authorities, regulations, and other security classification requirements as specified in the DD Form 254. The Government will not sponsor facility clearance upgrades or personnel clearance upgrades for the purpose of proposal submission or contract award eligibility. If your company is NOT requesting the classified source code, please state "Not Applicable" or "N/A" for these fields. SOLICITATION ANNOUNCEMENT: AN/BYG-1 APPLICATIONS The Department of the Navy, Naval Sea Systems Command (NAVSEA), on behalf of the Portfolio Acquisition Executive for Undersea (PAE Undersea) and the Director, Submarine Programs (DSP), is releasing the formal solicitation for the AN/BYG-1 Applications requirement from the Submarine Combat and Weapons Control Program Office (PMS 425). This notice follows the previously published Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) and Industry Day event. The Government has reviewed the feedback received during and after the Industry Day and has revised the requirements accordingly for this final solicitation. SCOPE OF THE REQUIREMENT (GENERAL OVERVIEW) AN/BYG-1 is the U.S. Navy�s Submarine Combat Control System. The AN/BYG-1 provides tools for the analysis of surface, sub-surface, and airborne contacts operating in the vicinity of own-ship and within the mission theater. This analysis supports command and decision-making, payload and attack control functions, determination of ballistic data for legacy torpedoes, and initiation of firing sequence for all payload types in support of submarine mission areas. The scope of this solicitation encompasses the development, testing, integration, delivery, logistics, and full-lifecycle sustainment of compiled AN/BYG-1 software baselines. This includes current, future, and legacy AN/BYG-1 applications as part of a modernized capability delivery framework. Key objectives and technical efforts under this contract include: Deliver AN/BYG-1 capabilities and baselines in alignment with Submarine Tactical Requirements Group priorities Decouple AN/BYG-1 applications from hardware and software dependencies Implement microcontainer/microservices AN/BYG-1 architecture Transform AN/BYG-1 development and test environments by increasing virtualization and establishing a common, shared infrastructure Develop and integrate tactical decision aids that leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies Assist with the design, development, and integration of combat control system elements to support international cooperative agreements and joint programs. title: Acadia National Park
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for Acadia National Park, Project ME NP ACAD BRG(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000002, located in Hancock County, Maine. The project consists of repair of Main Route 233, Paradise Hill, and Frazer Creek Bridges. The work includes reconstruction of asphalt concrete pavement and aggregate base course, placement of structural backfill, cleaning and removing debris from weepholes and inlets, cleaning and sealing joints, erosion repair, repointing mortar joints, placing waterproofing membrane to improve the service life, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 9, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

description: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) is to issue this Request for Proposal (RFP) HM047626R0018 for public response for the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) Human Resource Management II (HRM II). The HRM II RFP will be a commercial effort under FAR Part 12, and the Government anticipates using Best Value � Tradeoff evaluation methods and acquisition procedures as described in FAR Part 15. Contract award will be made to the offeror who provides the best overall value to the Government in terms of evaluation factors listed in Section 5 of the RFP. The procurement will be conducted using full and open competition procedures. The Government contemplates award of a performance-based contract using Firm Fixed Price (FFP) and Time-and-Materials (T&M) CLINs resulting from the solicitation. The period performance is anticipated to be a one (1) year base period with four (4) twelve (12) month option periods. The HRM II acquisition includes: The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency requires comprehensive Human Resource Management support services across the employee lifecycle. The requirement includes support for functions such as personnel data processing, talent acquisition support, talent development support, strategic workforce planning, employee support services, performance records management, benefits processing, retirement tracking, and related HR management support activities. In order to be considered for this requirement, the offeror shall have an active registration in the System for Award Management (SAM), https://www.sam.gov. description: Objets des services du marché : DEVELOPPEMENT DE PROGRAMMES ET DE MODULES DE FORMATION EN E-LEARNING DANS LES THEMATIQUES DES MARCHES PUBLICS ET DE L’ORGANISATION FINANCIERE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. Le marché public est divisé en lots. Les soumissionnaires sont libres d’introduire une offre pour un ou pour plusieurs lots. L’ensemble des lots organisés par le présent marché visent à l’élaboration, la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement, la livraison, l’intégration avec support technique dans la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP ainsi que la maintenance de trois modules de formation/apprentissage au format e-learning, disponibles simultanément en versions française et néerlandaise. Les lots 1, 2 et 3 visent l’élaboration de trois programmes d’apprentissage (objectifs, contenus, dispositif pédagogique) rendus disponibles en langue française et destinés à s’intégrer dans des modules en e-learning. Ces 3 programmes portent sur les trois thématiques suivantes : - « Introduction aux achats publics des administrations communales et des CPAS bruxellois ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des administrations communales bruxelloises ». - « Introduction à l’organisation financière des CPAS bruxellois ». Les lots 4 et 5 visent la conception technique, la médiatisation, le développement technique et la maintenance des trois modules de formation au format e-learning sur base des trois programmes d’apprentissage susmentionnés. Hébergement des modules e-learning : les modules de formation e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS de l’ERAP (voir description technique en annexe). Le cas échéant, les modules e-learning seront hébergés sur la plateforme LMS d’un ou plusieurs administrations clientes ou sur un site Internet. Il est à noter que le présent marché ne couvre pas les services liés à l’intégration des modules e-learning sur d’autres plateformes que celle mise à disposition par l’ERAP. Durée des modules e-learning : Les modules de formation au format e-learning visés par les lots 4 et 5 ont une durée respective estimée à 60 minutes (2 x 30 min. ou 4 x 15 min.). Thématique des modules : Ces modules s’intègrent dans un parcours de formation plus large destiné à l’onboarding des agents de niveau A, B ou C des administrations communales et des CPAS de la Région de Bruxelles-capitale. Estimation du nombre d’utilisateurs finaux pour chacun des trois modules d’apprentissage : environ 550 personnes par an (500 apprenants/utilisateurs finaux et 50 responsables représentants les administrations concernées + personnel ERAP). Durée du marché : pour tous les lots, le marché est conclu pour une durée d’un an, renouvelable trois fois pour la même durée, pour une durée totale de 4 ans (voir point II.7 pour les détails). Le marché est divisé en lots de la manière suivante : (1) LOT 1 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (2) LOT 2 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES ADMINISTRATIONS COMMUNALES BRUXELLOISES. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (3) LOT 3 : ÉLABORATION D’UN PROGRAMME D’APPRENTISSAGE D’INTRODUCTION À L’ORGANISATION FINANCIÈRE DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS. CE PROGRAMME EST DISPONIBLE EN FRANÇAIS ET DESTINÉ À L’E-LEARNING ». (4) LOT 4 : CONCEPTION, MÉDIATISATION, DÉVELOPPEMENT, LIVRAISON, INTEGRATION DANS LA PLATEFORME LMS ERAP AVEC SUPPORT TECHNIQUE ET MAINTENANCE DU MODULE E-LEARNING D’INTRODUCTION AUX ACHATS PUBLICS DES COMMUNES ET DES CPAS BRUXELLOIS (DURÉE ESTIMÉE : 60 MINUTES), EN VERSIONS FRANÇAISE ET NÉERLANDAISE. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 4 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 Nov 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: Technical Area 1 (TA1) and Technical Area 2 (TA2) are structured as a Closed-Staggered, 2 Step BAA. Therefore, for TA1 and TA2 ONLY: The Government anticipates awarding two awards for Technical Area 1 and two awards for Technical Area 2. Therefore, white papers for TA1 and TA2 are due on 10 JAN 2022 and if requested, proposals are due on 25 FEB 2022. Please note that white papers will still be accepted for TA1 and TA2 after the 10 JAN 2022 date, however, the likelihood of funding being available is substantially reduced. For all other Technical Areas: The Government anticipates adding technical areas via BAA amendment in the future. All potential Offerors are requested to wait to submit white papers until the BAA announcement is updated with specific technology requirements and dates. Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the System for Award Management (SAM) website at https://sam.gov/ in the event this announcement is amended. The Fight Tonight Program Team anticipates hosting an Industry Day to provide interested offerors an opportunity to learn more about Fight Tonight activities. Due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, the Industry Day is anticipated to be offered both in-person and virtually. Details regarding time, place, registration, format, and attendee access will be published on SAM shortly following the announcement publication proper. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Rome, NY, is seeking innovative research that revolutionizes air operations planning by combining Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven planning with interactive gaming to significantly reduce the Air Tasking Order planning cycle. Human-guided AI will generate myriad potential courses of action and the gaming environment will allow operators to explore, cull, and evaluate combat plans, gaining insight into the future battlespace. The over-arching strategy of this five (5) year open BAA is to quickly and efficiently execute research and development to deliver practical solutions to urgent problems. These efforts are anticipated to entail rapidly integrating existing technology into field testable, functional prototypes of solutions to military problems in two (2) major Focus Areas: Technical Area 1 (TA1): Interactive Plan Refinement Technical Area 2 (TA2): Plan Gaming and Outcome Analysis This strategy provides AFRL Rome, NY a solicitation tool with the flexibility to solicit white papers and proposals for Contract or agreements to perform rapid prototyping of technical solutions to meet compelling Air Force needs. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 54 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $3M to $40M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. Any anticipated funding listed reflects estimated program funding only. This estimate is not a promise of funding. Funding is uncertain and is subject to change. Changes in availability may occur as a result of the exercise of Government discretion. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction Project NP NER PMS BMS FY24(1), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000003, located in Dutchess, Nassau, Suffolk and Saratoga Counties, New York; Sullivan County, New Hampshire; and Hampden County, Massachusetts. The project consists of bridge maintenance and pavement preservation of roadways and parking areas across several parks including Home of FDR National Historic Site (HOFR), Eleanor Roosevelt National Historic Site (ELRO), Vanderbuilt Mansion National Historic Site (VAMA), Fire Island National Seashore (FIIS), Saint Gaudens National Historic Park (SAGA), Sagamore Hill National Historic Park (SAHI), Saratoga National Historical Park (SARA) and Springfield Armory National Historical Park (SPAR). The work includes thin lift asphalt overlay, chip seal, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, pavement markings, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $2,000,000 to $3,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about October 29, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

title: Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction - NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2)
description: Sealed bids from certified Small Business Concerns only will be accepted for the Northeast Region Pavement and Bridge Preservation Construction, Project NP NER PMS BMS FY25(2), Solicitation Number 693C73-27-B-000004, located in Essex County, New Jersey; Pike, Wayne, and Lackawanna Counties, Pennsylvania; and the City of Baltimore, Maryland. The project consists of roadway and bridge maintenance at Thomas Edison National Historical Park (EDIS), Fort McHenry National Monument and Historic Shrine (FOMC), Steamtown National Historic Site (STEA), and Upper Delaware Scenic and Recreational River (UPDE). The work includes micro surfacing, thin lift asphalt overlay, crack cleaning and sealing, asphalt concrete pavement patching, milling and overlay, concrete repair, drainage repairs, speed bump replacement, concrete paver installation, pavement markings, minor bridge repairs, and other miscellaneous work. The project will be split into multiple work schedules/contract options, with the cost of the entire project expected to fall within the price range of $3,000,000 to $4,000,000. Bid documents should be issued on or about November 6, 2026. Bid due date and location will be specified on the SF 1442, Block 13a of the Solicitation. Use Internet address https://www.sam.gov (click on Contract Opportunities, then type �693C73� in the Search Contract Opportunities box and click the search button and all available projects will be listed) to check for the availability of advertisement documents. All documents can be directly downloaded from this website. Solicitation documents will not be mailed. Register to receive email notifications to be automatically notified when a document is added or updated for a specific project. If firms do not register as an interested vendor at this website, there will be no Interested Vendors List. Please send all questions concerning construction projects to eflhd.contracts@dot.gov. Include the solicitation number, project name and number, requesting firm and address, a point of contact and telephone number. Requests for 'faxing' or overnight mailing will not be accepted. IMPORTANT SAM REGISTRATION AND PAYMENT REQUIREMENTS In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 52.204-7 (DEVIATION NOV 2025), prospective contractors shall have an active Federal Government contracts registration in the System for Award Management (SAM) when submitting an offer in response to this solicitation and at the time of award. To register in SAM, go to https://www.sam.gov. Annual contractor representations and certifications must be completed online at https://www.sam.gov. Also, FAR 52.232-33 requires SAM registration for payment. The required annual Form VETS-4212 must also be completed online at http://www.dol.gov/vets/vets4212.htm per FAR 52.222-37. PLEASE NOTE For security reasons, individuals requiring access to all government buildings must present a valid photo ID and be escorted to their destination by a Government employee. All visitors attending bid openings are urged to arrive at least 1 hour prior to a scheduled bid opening. All visitors must sign in at the main entrance of the Quantum Park facility and wait to be escorted by a Government employee to Eastern Federal Lands Highway Division (EFLHD) in Suite 200. Visitors must then register with the EFLHD Receptionist. A Government employee will collect all bids. Prior to the bid opening, a Government employee will escort all bidders to the bid opening. Unescorted visitors will be denied entry and no exceptions will be made. Bidders are encouraged to submit bids electronically per the instructions provided in the solicitation.

title: Strategic Technology Office-wide Innovation Solutions Opening Announcement
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) anticipates funding a limited number of proposals under this solicitation. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. Proposed research should investigate innovative approaches that enable revolutionary advances in science, devices, or systems. The Strategic Technology Office (STO) at DARPA regularly publishes solicitations requesting responses to specific program topics. This announcement seeks revolutionary research ideas for topics not addressed by ongoing STO programs or other published DARPA solicitations. To avoid proposals that duplicate existing activities or are responsive to other published STO solicitations, potential proposers are highly encouraged to review current STO programs and solicitations, respectively listed at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/offices/sto and http://www.darpa.mil/work-with-us/opportunities. Contacting STO program managers to discuss their research interests is also encouraged. A current list of program managers is available at http://www.darpa.mil/about-us/people. This Innovation Solutions Opening solicits under the procurement authorities of 10 U.S. Code � 4001, 10 U.S.C. � 4021, 10 U.S.C. � 4022, and 10 U.S.C. � 4023, that allow procurement activities authority to enter into agreements with industry, academia, and other organizations to fund research and development through cooperative agreements, Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs) for research, OTAs for prototypes, and procurement for experimental purposes. Proposals received as a result of this Innovation Solutions Opening will be evaluated by the Government in accordance with the evaluation criteria specified herein through a scientific review process. DARPA solicitations are posted on the SAM website under the Contract Opportunities link at https://sam.gov/. The following information is for those wishing to respond to the Innovation Solutions Opening. 1.1. STO MISSION AND THRUST AREAS DARPA's STO is a systems warfare office that seeks innovative and disruptive technologies for existing and future battlespaces. STO programs deliver solutions at speed and scale for today's warfighters while developing the resilient "breakthrough" systems and technologies across all physical domains (Air, Space, Sea, and Land) and across the spectrum of competition. STO does not focus on one area of responsibility or phenomenology. Instead, STO programs capture the strategic, logistical, and tactical complexity of today's national security environments. STO seeks to create new "proof-of-concept" mission systems. 1.2. TOPIC AREAS OF INTEREST Research areas of current interest to STO include, but are not limited to, the following topics: � Acoustic communication and sensing � Adaptability � Advanced computing � Additive manufacturing � Architecture and advanced systems engineering � Artificial intelligence � Autonomy and control algorithms � Combat identification � Command and control (C2) � Communications and networking, virtual and adaptive � Complexity management � Critical infrastructure defense � Decision aids and C2 technology � DevOps and novel software development and integration � Directed energy (DE) � Distributed autonomy and teaming (machine-machine, human-machine) � Economic security � Effects chain functions (disaggregated find, fix, track, target, engage, assess) � Electro-optic/infrared sensors � Electromagnetic warfare (EW) � High-frequency (HF) communications and sensing � High voltage electric power systems and architecture � Human behavior modeling � Human-machine symbiosis � Industrial engineering � Integration and reliability technologies � Interoperability � Logistics � Modeling and simulation � Microwave and millimeter wave communications and sensing � Novel kinetic effects � Non-kinetic effects (EW, DE, cyber) � Optical technologies � Photonics � Radio technologies (especially software-defined and novel waveforms and processing) � Radar and adaptive arrays � Resilient systems � Robotics � Seekers and other expendable sensors and processing � Sensors and analytics � Signal processing � Space sensors, communications, autonomy, and architectures (especially supporting proliferated low earth orbit constellations) � Strategy analysis technology � Supply chain analytics � System of systems � Undersea and seabed technology � Tactics development technology � Testing and data collection � Very low earth orbit (VLEO) technology � Very low frequency (VLF) technology

title: Solicitation of a Concession Business Opportunity to Operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services within Lake Mead National Recreation Area
description: The National Park Service (NPS) has released on September 2, 2026, a business opportunity soliciting proposals to award a new ten (10) year concession contract to operate Guided Water Tours, Food & Beverage, and Retail Services in Lake Mead National Recreation Area. The NPS will host a site visit for entities interested in bidding on the opportunity on September 21, 2026. The site visit provides interested entities with an overview of the concession operation and a tour of the Concession Facilities (land and real property improvements assigned to the concessioner under the Draft Contract), as well as the Desert Princess vessel, which is government-owned personal property assigned to the concessioner. title: France – Public road transport services – DELEGATION DE SERVICE PUBLIC RELATIVE A LA GESTION ET L’EXPLOITATIONDES SERVICES DE MOBILITE ET DE TRANSPORT DE VOYAGEURS SUR LETERRITOIRE DE CHATEAUROUX METROPOLE
description: La consultation a pour objet de déléguer la gestion et l’exploitation des services de mobilité et de transport de voyageurs sur le ressort territorial de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole (Réseau Horizon) Châteauroux Métropole, autorité Organisatrice de la mobilité est autorité délégante. Les missions déléguées sont les suivantes: Offre de base : Exploitation et gestion des services de mobilité et de transports publics de personnes et à l’échelle du territoire communautaire selon les principes définis à l’article 5.1 du document programme. Les candidats devront obligatoirement répondre à l’offre de base et à l'option obligatoire.• Option obligatoire :Option N°1 : Exploitation et gestion d’un service de location de vélos L’option est décrite à l’article 5.2 du document programme. L’Autorité Délégante précisera, avant la remise de l'offre finale si l'option est levée. Le Délégataire assurera la gestion de ces services pour une durée de six (6) ans, à compter du 01/01/2028 et jusqu’au 31/12/2033 dans le cadre d’une délégation de service public (DSP) au sein du périmètre contractuel. Lieu d’exécution : Territoire de la Communauté d’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole(département de l’Indre). L’estimation de la valeur du contrat de concession est de 45 millions d’euros HT valeur décembre 2026 sur la durée du contrat. Les missions attendues sont l'organisation, la production et la commercialisation des services, ainsi que la réalisation de l'offre de transport et la maintenance des véhicules et outils de production.Le délégataire assurera en outre la gestion de la relation avec les usagers des transports scolaires qui sont assurés par le biais de marchés publics en cours. La future DSP intègre la gestion et l'exploitation des services de transport suivants sur l’ensemble du périmètre de l’Agglomération de Châteauroux Métropole : • Le réseau de transport en commun « Horizon » composé aujourd’hui de 12 lignes régulières, • Le service de transport adapté à la demande, « Handibus », à destination des personnes à mobilité réduite sur le périmètre de CM .Pour cette gestion déléguée, la collectivité met à la disposition du délégataire : • Un dépôt de bus réceptionné en 2021 avec une capacité de stationnement de 80 véhicules, équipé de bureaux, d’un atelier de maintenance, de stations de lavage et de carburant et d’équipements de recharge de véhicule électrique; • 31 autobus standard, 5 autobus articulé, 2 midibus. Ces véhicules sont équipés d’équipements de suivi par système SAEIV et cellules de comptage voyageurs. Plusieurs véhicules standard et articulés électriques ont également été commandés. • 2 midibus accessibles et équipés pour accueillir des PMR • Un Site Internet https://www.bushorizon.com/ La présente concession est passée sur le fondement du règlement 1370/2007 et de la directive 2014/23/CEE. La directive 2014/25/UE citée dans le présent avis concerne les marchés des secteurs spéciaux est non les concessions , elle ne s'applique pas à la présente consultation.

title: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND NEXT GENERATION DISTRIBUTED COMMAND AND CONTROL
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Artificial Intelligence and Next Generation Distributed Command and Control BAA NUMBER: FA8750-23-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 AUG 2028. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 48 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $200K to $20M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. However, the Air Force reserves the right to award zero, one, or more Procurement Contracts, Other Transactions, or Assistance Instruments, for all, some, or none of the solicited effort based on the offeror�s ability to perform desired work and funding fluctuations. There is no limit on the number of OTs that may be awarded to an individual offeror. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: FAR based Procurement contracts, DODGARS based grants and cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) under 10 USC 4021, 10 USC 4022 and 10 USC 4023 (previously 10 USC 4002, 2371, 10 USC 4003, 2371b and 4004, 2373) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype Agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Gennady Staskevich AFRL/RISC 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315) 330-4889 Email: gennady.staskevich@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below (email requests are preferred): Amber Buckley Telephone (315) 330-3605 Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 1600 hours Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 AUG 2028, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY24 by 13 SEP 2023 FY25 by 15 Mar 2024 FY26 by 15 Mar 2025 FY27 by 15 Mar 2026 FY28 by 15 Mar 2027 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the SAM website at https://SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds great potential in transforming the Department of the Air Force (DAF) and Joint Force Command and Control (C2) capabilities across strategic, operational, and tactical levels by enabling decision makers to effectively assess the battlespace, rapidly explore, create, and select the best plan, and direct and monitor forces at pace and scale in a distributed setting. This BAA is interested in exploring new and advancing existing AI and distributed C2 concepts. By accelerating the research & development of novel AI-based and distributed capabilities to support Joint All Domain C2, the DAF can achieve a strategic decision advantage, where AI becomes a key and prevalent component to future C2 systems. With the rise of AI-based applications also comes new challenges to include the ability to effectively manage, monitor, and adapt deployed AI capabilities and effective C2 in a distributed and contested environment. Distributed operations is a critical component of Next-Generation C2. Key to the DAF transitioning from a single monolithic C2 node to multiple distributed C2 nodes is the ability orchestrate operational processes, while optimizing for limited resources. Through the development of distributed C2 capabilities the DAF can achieve an agile, fully mobile, distributed, and virtualized C2 operational capability. This BAA is interested in key areas for advancing C2 capability for the DAF to include but not limited to development and application of AI to C2, new concepts and techniques for the battle management and orchestration of AI at pace and scale, how the use of AI by adversaries can be considered in the C2 planning and execution process and distributed and collaborative C2 to enable C2 anywhere and anyplace. title: Netherlands, Germany – Industry specific software development services – Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program (Dynamic Purchasing System - EU-404)
description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.

title: France – Advertising and marketing services – Prestations de communication numérique touristique et d'attractivité-.
description: Le présent marché a pour objet la structuration et la planification d’une communication numérique dédiée à la promotion des atouts touristiques de Troyes Champagne Métropole. Cette stratégie doit reposer principalement sur un vécu expérientiel dans lequel les prospects et repeaters (visiteurs récurrents) vont se projeter et s’identifier. Pour ce faire, les prestations attendues au titre de ce marché reposent sur une stratégie de promotion numérique sur Internet et les réseaux sociaux (dont ceux de l’Office du tourisme, de la ville de Troyes et de Troyes Champagne Métropole) et pouvant être déclinés en spots télévisés segmentés et replay. Conformément à l’article L2113-10 du Code de la commande publique, la présente consultation est allotie comme suit : Lot n°1 : Création et mise au format de visuels publicitaires ; Lot n°2 : Réalisation de vidéos et prise de photos ; Lot n°3 : Média planning et stratégie de diffusion numérique ; En application de l’article R2113-1 du Code de la commande publique, les opérateurs économiques peuvent soumissionner pour les 3 lots. Les 3 lots susvisés peuvent être attribués à un seul et même opérateur économique. Conformément aux dispositions des articles L2125-1.1°, R. 2162-1 à R. 2162-6 et R. 2162-13 à R. 2162-14 du Code de la Commande Publique, chaque lot donnera lieu, à la conclusion d’un accord-cadre mono-attributaire à bons de commande. Le titulaire de l’accord-cadre sera consulté, à chaque survenance d’un besoin, par le biais de l’émission de bons de commande, conformément aux dispositions des articles R. 2162-13 et R. 2162-14 du Code de la Commande Publique. En application de l’article R.2162-4-2° du Code de la Commande Publique, l’accord-cadre sera conclu avec les montants maximum suivants : - S’agissant du lot n°1 : un montant maximum de 40 000 € HT annuel ; - S’agissant du lot n°2 : un montant maximum de 60 000 € HT annuel ; - S’agissant du lot n°3 : un montant maximum de 80 000 € HT annuel. Pour chaque lot, la durée de validité du présent marché court à compter de sa date de notification pour une durée d’un an. Celui-ci est reconductible, 3 fois par voie tacite, par période de 12 mois. Le titulaire du marché public ne pourra refuser la reconduction conformément aux dispositions de l’article R2112-4 du Code de la commande publique. En cas de non-reconduction, un courrier sera adressé au(x) titulaire(s) du marché public au moins un mois avant l’échéance de ce dernier. Pour chaque lot, les délais d’exécution seront fixés au sein de chaque bon de commande.

title: Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking (SARSAT) United States Mission Control Center (USMCC) Operations, Maintenance, and Technical Support
description: Operations, Maintenance, and Sustainment Support of the Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking (SARSAT) United States Mission Control Center (USMCC) Sources Sought Notice This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is issued solely for market research purposes to identify capable small and large business entities and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ). This notice does not represent a commitment on the part of the Government to award a contract, nor shall the Government incur any financial obligation for information submitted in response hereto. No claim against the Government may arise from a response to this SSN or from the Government's use of any submitted information. Failure to respond to this SSN does not prohibit participation in any potential subsequent solicitation. The information contained herein is subject to revision and imposes no binding obligation upon the Government. All submitted materials shall become the property of the Government and will not be returned. Any proprietary or copyrighted information included in a response must be explicitly marked as such. Requirement: This notice is issued by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) National Environmental Satellite, Data, and Information System (NESDIS), Office of Satellite and Mission Operations (OSPO) to identify sources capable of providing 24x7x365 Operations, Maintenance, and Sustainment Support of the Search and Rescue Satellite-Aided Tracking (SARSAT) United States Mission Control Center (USMCC). The SARSAT system relays distress signals from distress beacons carried by aviators, mariners and land-based users to Search and Rescue (SAR) services. The anticipated period of performance is a base year plus four option years. The mission of the interagency SARSAT program is to: Protect life and property by providing accurate, timely, and reliable distress alert and location information to search and rescue authorities. The U.S. SARSAT Program Management Office manages, coordinates, and implements the United States activities in the international Cospas- Sarsat search and rescue program. The mission of the SARSAT Program is fulfilled by: Collecting and distributing reliable and accurate distress alert data in a timely fashion using satellite receiving stations and a mission control center. Coordinating with national and international organizations on frequency management, satellite, emergency beacon and search and rescue issues. Maintaining a national register for 406 MHz emergency beacons. Operating, maintaining and improving the U.S SARSAT System, and representing the United States to the International Cospas-Sarsat Program. Please refer to the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) for detailed requirements description. NAICS Code/Size Standard: The applicable NAICS code is 541715, Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology). Key Criteria: Provide 24x7x365 operation support for the USMCC, leveraging subject matter expertise to collect and distribute accurate, timely, reliable alert data. Core responsibilities include: Monitoring and operating remote satellite receiving stations as well as the mission control center. Maintaining and managing the national 406 MHz emergency beacon database. Delivering customer support and quality assurance for new and existing beacon registrations. Demonstrate comprehensive expertise and in-depth knowledge of both the domestic U.S. SARSAT initiative and the International Cospas-Sarsat Program. Coordinate frequency management, satellites, emergency beacons, and search and rescue matters with key partners: National Organization: NASA, USCG, USAF, FAA, FCC, and related agencies. International Organizations: COSPAS-SARSAT, ITU, IMO, ICAO, EUMETSAT, RTCM, RTCA, and other global bodies. Provide comprehensive technical and programmatic support to the lead U.S. agency for the U.S. SARSAT Program, while representing the United States within the international Cospas-Sarsat Program. Core support includes managing event logistics and delivering both on-site and remote meeting support for domestic and international conferences hosted on behalf of the U.S. Government. Demonstrate working knowledge of the DOC and NOAA IT security requirements for maintaining, operating, and possibly transitioning a critical national system. Required Response Information: Capable small and large business vendors are requested to provide the following information in response to this SSN announcement: Company Name/Division, mailing address, e-mail address, telephone number, and website URL (if available). A single Point-of-Contact name, title, telephone number, and e-mail address. Unique Entity ID (UEI). Please note that companies must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) to be considered potential sources (SAM.gov). Business Size in relation to NAICS 541715 and any SBA socio-economic certifications. Demonstrated capabilities in meeting the needs of the Key Criteria listed above. Government-Wide Contract Vehicles (e.g. GSA Advantage, NASA SEWP and/or any NOAA-Awarded Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity contracts) that can support the SARSAT USMCC requirements. Please confirm whether your organization intends to submit a proposal for this requirement, and specify if you will be participating as a prime or as a subcontractor. Conflict of Interest: Please detail the extent to which the respondent is aware of any potential organizational conflict of interest issues related to this requirement. Response Format: In order to better assist in the review of responses to this SSN, respondents are encouraged to prepare a capabilities statement that does not exceed 15 pages. Response Submission Requirements and Deadline: Responses to this SSN should be submitted via e-mail attachments, received no later than 05:00 PM, EST, 28 October 2026 to: Contracting Officer: Trang Tran at Trang.tran@noaa.gov; and Contracting Specialist: Scott DeLoera at Scott.deLoera@noaa.gov.

description: Description: Mortgage-Backed Securities Operations & Analytics (MBSOA) The Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) is issuing this Sources Sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support this requirement for providing Mortgage-Backed Securities Operations & Analytics (MBSOA) in Support of the Government National Mortgage Association (Ginnie Mae) Office of Securities Operations (OSO). The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and Product Service Code (PSC) assigned to this procurement are: 541512 � Computer System Design Services with a size standard of $34M; and DA01 - IT And Telecom - Business Application/Application Development Support Services (Labor) There is no solicitation at this time.
