title: MTEC Solicitation Summary: Fiscal Year 2026 Multi-Topic Request for Project Proposals
description: **********A summary of Amendment 01 to this Request for Project Proposals has been posted to SAM.gov on 09 October 2026. The only change incorporated within this summary announcement is the addition of Focus Area 16 ("Multisite Clinical Biomarker Platform for Trauma-Related Lung and Kidney Failure"). The full version of the amendment (as well as the original RPP) is available on MTEC's website (https://mtec-sc.org/) and includes additional changes/updates.********** The Medical Technology Enterprise Consortium (MTEC) is excited to post this summary announcement for a Request for Project Proposals (RPP) soliciting a broad range of medical prototype technological and knowledge solutions related to the Focus Areas of Interest (also called �Focus Area(s)�) listed below. Proposed solutions may include medical techniques, knowledge products, and materiel (e.g., medical devices, drugs, and biologics). Military relevance is a key feature of this RPP. Awards resulting from this RPP are expected to be made under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 4022 (Authority of the Department of Defense to carry out certain prototype projects). As stated at the end of this announcement, the full RPP is posted to the MTEC website (https://mtec-sc.org/); this notice is intended only to notify interested parties of the available solicitation. ____________________________________________________________________________________ Background: Current wartime operations assume that the United States and our allies will maintain air, land, maritime, space and cyber superiority. Future conflicts against peer and near-peer adversaries are expected to be layered stand-offs and fought across multiple domains. Mission success will be determined by our ability to compete to expand the competitive space, penetrate both strategically and operationally, disintegrate enemy�s defenses, exploit enemy weaknesses, and re-compete to consolidate gains. Medical capabilities play a critical role in each aspect of the future battlespace and must modernize rapidly to maintain Force readiness and increase soldier lethality. Focus Areas: To meet the intent of the RPP, each Enhanced White Paper proposal SHALL specifically address ONLY ONE Focus Area described below. Offerors are not limited to a single Enhanced White Paper proposal submission. Projects that fail to align with only one of these Focus Areas may not be considered for funding. The following Focus Areas of Interest are not listed in order of importance; the detailed requirements for each are described in the full version of the Request for Project Proposals. Focus Area 1: Policies and practices for cross-cutting prevention � the aim of this focus area is to develop and evaluate non-training interventions/activities that address risk and protective factors for harmful behaviors. Priority risk/protective factors to address include: morale, fairness, work-life balance, passive leadership, toxic leadership, and workplace hostility. Focus Area 2: Fostering Service member physical fitness through integrated primary prevention � the aim of this focus area is to develop interventions or trainings to combat the key contributors to force readiness and physical fitness. This focus area encourages offerors to consider resource/environmental constraints and social and psychological barriers present for warfighters when developing solutions. Focus Area 3: Identify and reduce barriers to help-seeking � the aim of this focus area is to identify and develop prototypes against key drivers of help-seeking. Proposed prototypes should prioritize high-impact resources/services and Service member populations at elevated risk for harmful behaviors. Focus Area 4: Prophylactic Solutions to Prevent Battlefield and Complex Traumatic Wound Infections in Austere or Contested Environments � the aim of this focus area is the development of prototypes to prevent or delay wound infections (bacterial, fungal, and/or antimicrobial-resistant) following battlefield and complex traumatic wounds, including in austere or contested environments, for use at the point of injury and in prolonged care environments (Roles 1 and 2), without negatively impacting wound healing. High-priority pathogens include Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Acinetobacter baumannii, Staphylococcus aureus, and invasive fungal infections. NOTE: This focus area is not interested in vaccines, burn wound solutions, or discovery-stage efforts. Focus Area 5: Pathogen Agnostic Countermeasures for the Treatment of Sepsis Caused by Wound Infection � the aim of this focus area is the development of products, including immune modulators, novel drugs, immunotherapeutics, and other pathogen-agnostic and/or host-directed prototypes, to treat sepsis following battlefield and complex traumatic wounds (excluding burn wounds), including in austere or contested environments. NOTE: This focus area is not interested in vaccines, burn wound solutions, discovery-stage efforts, or proposals focused solely on direct treatment of wound infection rather than sepsis. Focus Area 6: Knowledge Product Prototypes for the Prevention of Infection in Traumatic Penetrating Wounds � the aim of this focus area is the development of knowledge product prototypes to optimize clinical practice guidelines for the prevention of infection in traumatic penetrating wounds. Focus Area 7: Bacterial Diarrhea Prevention � the aim of this focus area is the development of prototypes to prevent bacterial diarrhea resulting from high-priority pathogens (Campylobacter jejuni, enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli, and Shigella) in operational settings. NOTE: Proposals targeting other pathogens will be deemed out of scope. Furthermore, this focus area will not consider proposals for vaccine-based interventions. Focus Area 8: Dengue Fever Prevention and/or Treatment Solutions � the aim of this focus area is the development of drugs and vaccines to prevent or treat all four serotypes of Dengue Fever. NOTE: Intravenous (IV) solutions are explicitly excluded and will not be considered under this Focus Area. Focus Area 9: Prevention and Treatment of Emerging Infectious Diseases � the aim of this focus area is on developing pathogen-agnostic and/or broad-spectrum solutions for prevention or treatment of Lassa fever virus, Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus (CCHFV), and various hantaviruses, which are high-consequence pathogens that pose distinct risks to the deployed Joint Force. NOTE: IV solutions as well as proposals focused solely on other pathogens, including endemic and emerging respiratory viruses, are explicitly excluded and will not be considered under this Focus Area. Focus Area 10: Musculoskeletal Injury Treatment � the aim of this focus area is the development of prototypes for musculoskeletal injury interventions for the pre-hospital environment. Specifically, this focus area seeks (1) therapeutic interventions to accelerate recovery from musculoskeletal injury or (2) solutions for the preservation of musculoskeletal health. To meet the intent of the funding opportunity, Enhanced White Papers submitted to this Focus Area must address ONLY one of the above listed sub areas. Focus Area 11: Operational Suitability of Existing Pain Treatments � the aim of this focus area is for the development of a knowledge product to generate definitive human performance data to inform risk/benefit decisions and create evidence-based recommendations for the Joint Trauma System (JTS) to refine and optimize existing Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPGs) and Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) protocols. Focus Area 12: Repurposing and Novel Delivery of Approved Compounds � the aim of this focus area is to accelerate the development of safer, opioid-sparing analgesics by leveraging the FDA's 505(b)(2) regulatory pathway for repurposed drugs delivered via novel administration methods. The desired end-state is a candidate drug/device combination ready to enter Phase I clinical

title: 6515--Inventory Management System
description: THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ISSUED SOLELY FOR INFORMATION AND PLANNING PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION. SUBMISSION OF INFORMATION ABOUT PRICING, DELIVERY, THE MARKET, AND CAPABILITIES IS HIGHLY ENCOURAGED AND ALLOWED UNDER THIS RFI FOR PLANNING PURPOSES IN ACCORDANCE WITH (IAW) FAR 15.201(e). DISCLAIMER This RFI is issued solely for information and planning purposes and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled accordingly. IAW FAR 15.201(e), responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI. SOURCES SOUGHT/RFI DESCRIPTION This is NOT a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice / RFI only. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice / RFI is to gain information about potential qualified sources and their size classification relative to NAICS code is 334519 - Other Measuring and Controlling Device Manufacturing, with an SBA small business size standard of 600 employees. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI will be used by the Government to make appropriate acquisition decisions. After review of the responses to this Sources Sought Notice / RFI, further RFIs and/or a solicitation or other announcements may be published. The purpose of this procurement is to acquire and install a fully automated, weight-based inventory management system, brand name or equal to PAR Excellence, for the VA Phoenix Healthcare System. The system is intended to provide accurate, real-time perpetual inventory visibility while minimizing end-user data entry and supporting timely replenishment of medical and surgical supplies. The anticipated requirement includes all equipment, scales, controllers, storage products, mounting hardware and accessories, software licenses, interfaces, implementation services, installation, configuration, testing, training, warranty, monitoring, maintenance, and technical support necessary to deliver a fully operational system at the facility's designated primary and secondary supply locations. For market-research and planning purposes, the anticipated configuration is approximately 26 PAR Bins Replenish software licenses, 3,571 scales of various types and capacities, 27 Ethernet replenishment controllers, related hardware accessories, storage bins, shelving, cabinets, mobile louvered panel units, and associated implementation and training services. Final quantities and configurations are subject to change. At a minimum, the proposed solution must provide an HL7 interface that communicates with the VA Generic Inventory Package (GIP) in VistA and must have an approved VA Information Technology Authority to Operate (ATO) at the time of offer. Contractors must be able to validate interoperability with VA GIP through the HL7 interface prior to award. The system must support unlimited users and multiple permission levels; provide access from multiple points on VA-furnished computers; produce Excel or text-delimited reports; display equipment and materials-management status; provide item-location, PAR-level analysis, consumption data, order, reconciliation, due-in/due-out, discrepancy, and inventory-value reporting; and generate pick-ticket information based on PAR levels, reorder points, and emergency stock levels. The system must be compatible with existing shelving, cabinets, carts, and other storage infrastructure; accommodate medical and surgical products of varying size, thickness, and weight, including products up to approximately 3 feet long by 2 feet wide and 20 pounds; and permit VA employees to recalibrate the system for different package quantities. The contractor must install and configure the required software on VA-furnished equipment, provide staff training, furnish a one-year license agreement with software upgrades, and provide 24 hours per day, 7 days per week, 365 days per year support. Support must include at least four remote equipment-functionality checks every 24 hours, response to service calls within 24 hours, and repair or replacement of covered equipment or hardware within 48 hours when damage or defect is not attributable to VA personnel. Installation is anticipated to begin no later than 70 days after contract award and be completed no later than 400 days after award, subject to facility deployment planning and required facility tasks. Deliverables will be shipped to VA Phoenix Healthcare System, Main Warehouse (ATTN: Prentiss Logan), 650 E Indian School Road, Phoenix, AZ 85012, with notice to the Contracting Officer's Representative five business days before shipment. The current independent planning estimate derived from the attached vendor quotation is $1,502,945.49, inclusive of turnkey installation. This amount is provided solely to describe the anticipated magnitude of the requirement for market-research purposes and does not constitute a Government estimate, commitment, or solicitation price. STATEMENT OF WORK 1. Background VA Phoenix Healthcare System has used cabinet-based Point of Use (POU) systems to manage inventory levels within our facility s supply areas. Our facility s current supply system process relies heavily on clinical staff entering quantities as they pull product. When they fail to enter, or enter incorrect quantities, our process fails. This leads to workload issues, as Supply Techs must be pulled from current duties to perform urgent resupply requests to affected areas. This also presents potential patient safety issues during emergency situations if stock is not available due to inaccurate stock level information. Further, the current supply process is labor and time intensive. This is compounded in times of heavy workload due to availability of supply personnel and/or hospital patient load, increasing risks associated with patient care / safety. VA Phoenix Healthcare System is looking for a fully automated weight-based inventory management system that does not require end users to input data or interface with the system to increase or decrease material items stocked or consumed by the user. The station requires a system that removes or heavily limits the amount of human interface required to maintain accurate and real time inventories. This creates a more accurate and efficient system while simultaneously addressing the patient safety / care concerns mentioned above, eliminating the frequent emergent supply requests created by inadequate inventory management systems. A fully automated weight-based inventory management system will augment the supply chain s management effectiveness and timeliness with resupply inventory while decreasing the workload of supply personnel. It will also improve the overall patient care throughout the facility, particularly in the cardiac catheterization and electrophysiology labs, by effectively maintaining appropriate periodic automatic replacement levels. 2. Scope The scope of this requirement is to obtain and install an automated inventory management system at VA Phoenix Healthcare System, ensure system is fully operational, and fully train staff to be knowledgeable on the use of system. This is a brand name or equal requirement; a Fully Automated Weight-Based Inventory Management System or equal to PAR Excellence. Contractors must provide a brand name or equal that meets or exceeds the physical, functional, and performance of listed characteristics described in this Statement of Work. Contractor must show clear and compelling, and convincing evidence that all equal to items meet all required salient characteristics including brand name and model numbers IAW FAR 52.211-6 Brand Name or Equal. title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption and Implementation Support Services
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) requires a structured artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and implementation-support program to assist multiple PSPC organizations in identifying, assessing, prioritizing, and planning the implementation of AI opportunities within their business areas. The requirement consists of a coordinated twelve-month pilot involving multiple participating PSPC groups. The successful supplier will provide a structured program that combines advisory support, facilitated learning, readiness assessments, implementation planning, knowledge transfer, and ongoing participant engagement. The work includes, but is not limited to: Identifying and evaluating operational opportunities for AI adoption; Supporting the assessment and prioritization of AI use cases; Conducting organizational readiness and implementation assessments; Facilitating workshops, learning sessions, and collaborative activities; Providing ongoing advisory support and guidance throughout the pilot period; Supporting participating groups in progressing from opportunity identification to implementation planning; Facilitating knowledge sharing and peer learning among participating groups; Building internal organizational capacity for responsible AI adoption; and Developing repeatable practices, lessons learned, and implementation approaches that may support future AI adoption initiatives. The objective of the pilot is to advance organizational readiness for AI adoption while supporting participating groups in developing practical and implementable AI opportunities through a common framework and coordinated approach.

title: Germany – IT services: consulting, software development, Internet and support – Einführung von Ki in der Eingangsverarbeitung
description: Gegenstand des Verfahrens: Der Beitragsservice von ARD, ZDF und Deutschlandradio beschafft einen KI-basierten Service zur automatisierten Verarbeitung eingehender schriftlicher Sendungen (Papier/Scan, E-Mail, Fax), der als Managed Service (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS) auf einer souveränen Cloud betrieben werden soll. Der KI-Service klassifiziert die Sendungen nach der Dokumentart-Systematik des Beitragsservice (DAK/SDAK), erkennt das fachliche Anliegen und extrahiert die für die Weiterverarbeitung erforderlichen Fachdaten. Die Ergebnisse werden jeweils mit einem Confidence-Score als strukturierte JSON-Objekte an den bestehenden Verarbeitungsprozess zurückgegeben. Der KI-Service wird nicht als Ersatz, sondern als Bypass zur bestehenden Eingangsverarbeitung eingeführt. Die Aussteuerung der Sendungen erfolgt über vom Beitragsservice bereitgestellte intelligente Weichen; die Kernsysteme bleiben unverändert. Nicht Gegenstand der Ausschreibung sind das Scannen bzw. die Digitalisierung der Sendungen, die Ein- und Ausgangsschnittstellen der Gesamt-Eingangsverarbeitung sowie die intelligenten Weichen selbst. Der Leistungsgegenstand gliedert sich in drei Bausteine: Baustein 1 - Cloud-Infrastruktur: Bereitstellung einer souveränen, hochverfügbaren und skalierbaren Cloud-Umgebung als IaaS einschließlich bedarfsgerecht skalierbarer CPU-, GPU-, Speicher- und Netzwerkressourcen für KI-Workloads. Es ist beabsichtigt, einen Vertrag über die Bausteine 1 und 2 mit einer 4-jährigen Festlaufzeit abzuschließen. Baustein 2 - Managed Service: Betrieb der KI-Plattform als PaaS und SaaS, insbesondere Monitoring, Logging, Incident- und Problem-Management, Patch- und Release-Management, Backup und Recovery, Kapazitätsmanagement sowie Bereitstellung und Betrieb eines standardisierten KI-Serving-Stacks (u. a. Container-Orchestrierung, Inferenz). Der Beitragsservice behält die Hoheit über Fachlogik, Agenten sowie Auswahl und Wechsel der KI-Modelle. Es ist beabsichtigt, einen Vertrag über die Bausteine 1 und 2 mit einer 4-jährigen Festlaufzeit abzuschließen. Baustein 3 - Entwicklung einer individuellen Input-Management-Lösung ("KI-Service"): Konzeption, Entwicklung, Integration und Produktivsetzung einer individuellen Lösung auf Basis der bereitgestellten Plattform, einschließlich Einrichtung von Klassifikation und Extraktion je Sachverhalt, Nachweis der vereinbarten Erkennungsqualität, Schulung, Dokumentation und Unterstützung der Abnahme. Der KI-Service inkl. sämtlicher Arbeitsergebnisse (u. a. Quellcode, Konfigurationen, Prompt-Artefakte, Datenmodelle, Schnittstellenbeschreibungen, Tests, Dokumentation) geht mit zeitlich, räumlich und inhaltlich unbeschränkten Nutzungsrechten auf den Beitragsservice über. Dem Beitragsservice ist zudem das Recht einzuräumen, den KI-Service uneingeschränkt zu nutzen, zu betreiben, zu verändern und weiterzuentwickeln sowie durch Dritte betreiben oder weiterentwickeln lassen können. Es darf keine Abhängigkeit vom ursprünglichen Auftragnehmer entstehen und ein Anbieterwechsel muss grundsätzlich möglich sein. Die Lösung ist vorrangig auf Basis von Open-Source-Komponenten mit permissiven Lizenzen zu realisieren. Ergänzend ist ein Dienstleistungskontingent für weitere Sachverhalte vergleichbarer Komplexität und für Optimierungen nach der Produktivnahme bzw. Abnahme vorzusehen. Fachlicher Umfang und Mengengerüst: Schwerpunkt sind rund 1,8 Mio. formlose Schreiben pro Jahr, die bislang weder automatisch klassifiziert noch inhaltlich ausgewertet werden. Hinzu kommen rund 4,7 Mio. formgebundene Schreiben aus fünf Sachverhalten: Befreiungen, Abmeldungen, Drittschuldnererklärungen, Klärungsverfahren aufgrund Sterbefall sowie Bank- und Adressänderungen. Für die Dimensionierung ist von mindestens 6,5 Mio. Sendungen pro Jahr auszugehen (ca. 25.000 Sendungen je Arbeitstag, Spitzenwert ca. 26.700). Der Handschriftanteil liegt bei ca. 20 %. Teilweise sind besondere Kategorien personenbezogener Daten nach Art. 9 DSGVO (z. B. Gesundheitsangaben) zu verarbeiten. Wesentliche funktionale Anforderungen sind insbesondere: - KI-gestützte Texterkennung (OCR) über den gesamten Dokumentinhalt einschließlich mehrseitiger Dokumente und Anlagen; - inhaltsbasierte Klassifikation und Anliegenerkennung mittels Textverständnis statt Formularankern, einschließlich Erkennung mehrerer Anliegen je Sendung und Trennung mehrerer Dokumente; - Extraktion der Identifikationsfelder (u. a. Beitragsnummer, Name, Anschrift) und der je Sachverhalt benötigten Fachdaten, auch aus beigefügten Nachweisen; - Erkennung handschriftlicher Inhalte einschließlich freier Randnotizen, Ankreuzfelder und Prüfung auf Vorhandensein von Unterschriften; - Confidence-Scores je Ergebnis und Feld; keine Übernahme nicht belegbarer Inhalte; Schutz vor Prompt Injection; - integrierter Human-in-the-Loop-Pfad mit konfigurierbaren Aussteuerungsregeln und einer barrierefreien (BITV 2.0), deutschsprachigen, vollständig tastaturbedienbaren Nachbearbeitungsoberfläche; - Aufnahme weiterer Dokumentklassen ohne Neuaufsatz des Systems durch den Beitragsservice selbst; kein Training von Modellgewichten mit personenbezogenen Daten der Beitragszahlenden; - modellagnostische Architektur (vorzugsweise Open-Weight-Modelle), REST-Schnittstellen, Container-/Microservice-Architektur, UTF-8, Reporting (u. a. Precision/Recall/F1 je Dokumentklasse) und Anbindung an die Monitoring-Werkzeuge des Beitragsservice. Die Beschreibung der ausgeschriebenen Leistungen wird unter Ziffer 5.1. dieser Bekanntmachung fortgesetzt.

title: Belgium – Custom software development services – Vernieuwing en functionele uitbreiding van de „Espace Personnel“ – Oplossing voor de digitalisering van administratieve procedures voor burgers van de gemeente Schaerbeek
description: Le présent marché a pour objet le renouvellement et l'extension fonctionnelle de l'Espace Personnel, la plateforme numérique de dématérialisation des démarches administratives citoyennes de l'Administration communale de Schaerbeek. Il fait suite au marché attribué en 2021 (référence : scha/equip/2021/034), arrivé à échéance, et vise à assurer la continuité du service tout en comblant les lacunes fonctionnelles identifiées au cours de la période d'exploitation. L'analyse de l'existant a mis en évidence les lacunes fonctionnelles suivantes dans la plateforme actuelle, auxquelles le présent marché apporte une réponse : ► Absence d'authentification forte via Itsme® ou eID pour les démarches nécessitant une identification certaine du citoyen. ► Absence de fiche citoyen 360° centralisant l'historique complet des démarches, échanges et documents d'un même citoyen. ► Absence d'intégration CRM permettant la liaison automatique des dossiers citoyens avec les outils de gestion de la relation client de la commune. Le présent marché couvre l'ensemble des composants suivants, qu'il s'agisse de fonctionnalités reconduites, améliorées ou nouvellement introduites : ► Un espace personnel citoyen (front-end) accessible via authentification forte (Itsme®/eID/CSAM) ► Un back-office de gestion collaborative des dossiers pour les agents communaux ► Un créateur de formulaires no-code/low-code avec gestion des conditions et validations ► Un moteur de workflow et de modélisation de processus conforme au standard BPMN 2.0 ► Une authentification SSO via Azure Active Directory pour les agents ► Une gestion granulaire des droits, rôles et accès par service et par type de démarche ► Une intégration CRM et des connecteurs d'interopérabilité (API REST, webhooks) Le marché comprend : la licence d'utilisation de la plateforme, la configuration et le paramétrage initial, la migration des données existantes le cas échéant, la formation des agents et administrateurs, la documentation complète, et la maintenance corrective et évolutive pendant la durée du contrat. La solution actuellement en production à la Commune de Schaerbeek repose sur un ensemble de composants techniques décrits en détail à la section D.0 — Contexte technique de l’existant.
